transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Lin (Novus - Head of ML), Mark Rivera (Novus - Platform), Priya Nair (Novus - Security), Evan Gomez (Novus - Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick agenda — alignment on success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist, benchmarking approach and timeline. daniel will drive the technical bits.
[00:18] Dr. Sarah: thanks maya. the main ask from our side is a POC to validate an open model for clinical note summarization and an initial triage classifier. critical we measure hallucination rate and domain accuracy. timeline: we want pilot results by end of august if possible.
[00:35] Daniel: great, that gives us about 6 weeks. doable if we scope the benchmark and datasets. can you confirm target latency / throughput constraints — are you optimizing for sub-200ms token latency or are you more throughput-oriented?
[00:50] Mark: for the user-facing summarization in our clinician UI, p99 response around 400ms for a 512-token output is acceptable; for batch triage runs we care about throughput — maybe 50 to 150 qps peak depending on batch windows.
[01:05] Priya: security note — all datasets will need to be de-identified. we also require SOC2 evidence, support for customer-managed keys (KMS), and audit logs for all requests.
[01:18] Maya: understood. from Redwood side we can run Hosted API for the benchmark and then propose Dedicated if isolation or latency warrants. we'll share SOC2 and KMS integration docs in the follow-up.
[01:32] Evan: one more — multilingual support. 10% of our notes are spanish, some are portuguese clinical snippets. we need to understand cross-lingual performance.
[01:44] Daniel: good flag. we'll include en/es test sets in the benchmark. for portuguese we'll include a small sample but won't be a blocker for the initial POC.

Summary and success criteria discussion:
[02:05] Maya: let's walk through success criteria — please correct or add.
[02:10] Maya: 1) Summarization ROUGE-L / clinical F1 >= baseline (your current model) or delta +5 points; 2) Hallucination rate < 3% on constrained test set; 3) Triage classifier precision/recall > 0.9 on positive cases; 4) latency p95/p99 within targets (p99 < 400ms for 512-token summarization); 5) Cost per 1k prompts under target (we'll capture target once you share current spend).
[02:40] Dr. Sarah: that looks right. our internal baseline is a fine-tuned 7B private model — so ideally we match that or beat it on clinical metrics.
[02:52] Mark: and we care about deterministic outputs for certain structured fields — medication list extraction should be accurate.

Workload sizing and benchmark plan:
[03:10] Daniel: on workload sizing, from your notes earlier we estimate baseline production is around 1.2M tokens/day and burst to 1.8–2M tokens/day for monthly peaks. can you confirm those numbers?
[03:25] Mark: yes that's accurate, those are aggregated across triage and summarization. typical RTT constraints per request are also correlated with the UI.
[03:34] Daniel: ok for the benchmark we'll run two experiments: 1) latency focused (single-tenant, 95/99 latency measurement with synthetic mix of summarization and small triage requests) and 2) throughput/cost run (continuous batching, 2-hour sustained run to capture cost per token and throughput). we'll do model side-by-side runs: Llama 2 13B (instruction-tuned), Mistral 7B Instruct, MPT-30B-Instruct, and Falcon 40B (open weights variant).
[04:05] Dr. Sarah: quick question — aren't Falcon and MPT less reliable on hallucinations in medical text? we saw noise in some prior tests.
[04:15] Daniel: yes there's a tradeoff. smaller models with strong instruction tuning like Mistral 7B often punch above weight for speed/cost but can hallucinate more on long-form clinical context. larger models like 30–40B tend to be more consistent but cost/latency increase. we'll measure hallucination using your clinical QA set and use a disagreement oracle to flag hallucinations.
[04:36] Maya: also note Redwood's runtime supports quantized execution and pinned KV-caching that can reduce latency for repeated contexts; that may let you use a larger model but keep p99 in range.
[04:48] Priya: what's KV-caching? is that the cache that stores previous patient context? we need clarity on data retention in cache for compliance.
[04:59] Daniel: yes, KV cache stores internal attention key/value state to speed up autoregressive generation; it's not persisted to disk in Hosted mode unless you opt for explicit caching — we'll note retention defaults in the security doc. for Private/Dedicated we can configure customer-managed cache retention and encryption with your KMS.

Model selection specifics and quality tradeoffs:
[05:30] Daniel: proposed shortlist rationale:
- Llama 2 13B: strong instruction-following, good community support; mid-tier cost/latency.
- Mistral 7B Instruct: best-in-class efficiency; low cost and low latency but watch for domain hallucinations.
- MPT-30B: strong at instruction tasks with helpful tokenization; good for structured outputs.
- Falcon 40B (open weights): high quality on long context but higher resource needs.
[06:05] Dr. Sarah: any recommendations on which to prioritize for clinical summarization?
[06:10] Daniel: prioritize Llama 2 13B and MPT-30B for summarization accuracy + structured extraction; include Mistral 7B as a low-cost baseline; Falcon 40B as an upper-bound test if latency/cost allow.
[06:23] Maya: we'll also provide a Redwood-verified performance profile for each model — expected latency p50/p95 on our hosting tiers so you can judge economics.

Multilingual and domain adaptation notes:
[06:40] Daniel: for Spanish we'll run the same evaluation metrics; if quality is low, quick adaptation options: light fine-tuning (LoRA) on 1–5k examples or prompt engineering with retrieval augmented generation (RAG) using your de-identified EHR snippets. both are feasible in the POC window but fine-tuning adds complexity and data preparation.
[07:05] Dr. Sarah: we'd prefer not to fine-tune during POC unless necessary. RAG sounds interesting — does Redwood support document retrieval and context windows?
[07:13] Daniel: yes, Redwood supports embeddings and a retrieval pipeline; we can plug in an external vector DB or use our hosted vector endpoints for the benchmark. retrieval will help reduce hallucination for domain-specific facts.

Security and compliance discussion:
[07:35] Priya: we'll need SOC2 + penetration test evidence, and the ability to audit request logs. for Hosted POC, can you guarantee that customer data is deleted after benchmark runs?
[07:48] Maya: yes, we have retention policies and can delete logs and cached artifacts post-POC. we'll send the exact retention workflow. for Dedicated/Private we can do an isolated environment and KMS integration.
[07:58] Priya: are there any third-party dependencies? e.g., do you rely on a public redis or any managed services where data passes through an external tenant?
[08:10] Daniel: we can provide an architecture diagram. Hosted uses our managed infra but it's single-tenant per customer on the request plane; for strict isolation we recommend Dedicated. we'll include a list of managed services in the security packet.

Benchmark logistics and timelines:
[08:30] Maya: proposed timeline:
- July 15: scoping call (today)
- July 18: Redwood shares SOW + pricing + security docs
- July 20: Redwood shares benchmark harness and synthetic workload generator
- July 22: Novus shares de-identified samples and evaluation scripts
- July 28: Pilot kick-off (2 weeks of runs)
- Aug 11: Results review and decision on Dedicated pilot/next steps
[08:55] Dr. Sarah: fits our internal timelines if we can get the artifacts by the 22nd.

Pricing and cost modeling (high level):
[09:10] Maya: high-level pricing we sent earlier — Hosted per-token + throughput-based tiers. Dedicated is monthly commit with lower unit cost for sustained runs. we'll send a cost projection (expected $/1k prompts) for each model based on Redwood-verified perf.
[09:28] Mark: rough budget for POC is allocated, but we need clear cost estimates to sign off.

Customer questions and clarifications:
[09:40] Dr. Sarah: on hallucination detection — do you have tooling to automatically surface likely hallucinations?
[09:46] Daniel: we have a lightweight hallucination detector that uses conservative heuristics and a disagreement oracle across models; for the POC we'll run human-in-the-loop annotations on flagged examples.
[09:58] Evan: will we be able to replay raw transcripts of requests for debugging?
[10:02] Maya: yes, for debugging we can provide sanitized traces; retention and access controls per Priya's guidance.

Closing and recap:
[10:15] Maya: recap: Redwood to share SOW/security by 7/18, SE to publish benchmark plan by 7/20, Novus to share datasets and evals by 7/22, pilot kick-off week of 7/28. models tested: Llama 2 13B, Mistral 7B, MPT-30B, Falcon 40B (opt). success criteria captured.
[10:38] Dr. Sarah: sounds good, thanks. we'll prioritize sending data and the baseline metrics.
[10:45] Priya: I'll review the security packet once you send it; expect follow-up questions.
[10:50] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the kick-off and the SOW.

Notes on transcription quality: some proper nouns and model names may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., 'Mistral' hear as 'mystrel' in an automated pass) — we'll attach original recording in CRM.

References mentioned:
- Redwood performance profiles (link to be sent)
- Novus baseline model details (internal)
- Benchmark harness (docs/links to be shared by Redwood SE)

End of transcript.
